question.worked_solution:
Note that plugging in $x=0$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{ln\,(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))}{\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[ln\,(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x))]}^{′}}{[\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)})}{2{sec}^{2}⁡(2x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4(0))}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4(0))})}{2{sec}^{2}⁡(2(0))} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{4(1)}{1+0})}{2(1)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
